conversation.content:
Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to experience a wide range of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a screening tool designed to help us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns related to your postpartum experience. The purpose of this assessment is to provide a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and emotions, and to help us work together to ensure you're receiving the best possible care during this critical period.

Please know that everything we discuss today is confidential and respected. I'm here to listen and support you without judgment, and I want you to feel comfortable sharing your honest thoughts and feelings with me. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of your emotional well-being over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to create a comfortable and non-intimidating atmosphere for our conversation.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things that usually bring you happiness, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or struggling to cope?

Honestly, it's been really tough. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most days. I'm exhausted all the time, and it's hard to find the energy to do anything, even things I used to love. I mean, I'm happy to see my baby smile and all, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, but most of the time, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. 

Sometimes, I get these thoughts that I'm not doing enough for my baby, or that I'm not a good enough mom, and it's hard to shake them off. It's like, I know I'm trying my best, but it doesn't feel like it's good enough. And it's not just about the baby - I feel like I've lost interest in things I used to enjoy, like reading or spending time with friends. It's all just feeling really overwhelming, and some days, it feels like it's all just too much to handle. 

I do have some good moments, though. Like, when my baby cuddles with me, it feels amazing, and for a little while, everything feels okay. But those moments are fleeting, and then I'm back to feeling anxious and unsure of myself. I guess that's just how it's been for me over the past week - a lot of ups and downs, and mostly just trying to get through each day without feeling too overwhelmed.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

That's not really been me lately. I mean, I'll laugh at something my baby does, like a cute facial expression or a silly sound, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. Most of the time, I just feel like I'm going through the motions and trying to get everything done, but I don't really feel like I'm enjoying myself or finding the humor in things like I used to. 

Sometimes, my husband will try to make me laugh or tell me a joke, and I'll smile or chuckle, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy, instead of actually feeling it. And that's hard for me, because I used to be a pretty lighthearted person, and now it feels like that part of me is just gone. 

It's not that I never laugh or smile, but it's just not as often as it used to be, and it doesn't feel as genuine. And when I do laugh, it's often just a distraction from all the other things that are worrying me, like my baby's safety or whether I'm doing everything right. So, yeah, I'd say that's not really been me lately - being able to laugh and see the funny side of things.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. To be honest, I've been feeling really anxious and overwhelmed by all the things I need to do, and I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or trying new restaurants, just feel like too much effort now. 

I mean, sometimes my husband will suggest we do something, like go for a walk or watch a movie, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but then I'll start worrying about all the things I need to do for the baby, or whether I'll be able to get her to sleep, or whether I'll be able to enjoy myself without feeling guilty about leaving her with someone else. And then it just feels like too much, and I don't end up looking forward to it at all. 

Even things that are supposed to be fun, like baby classes or playdates, just feel like obligations now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to do all the "right" things for my baby, but I'm not really enjoying any of it. And that's hard for me, because I used to be someone who loved trying new things and looking forward to events and activities. Now, it all just feels like a chore. 

Sometimes, I'll see other moms on social media, and they'll be talking about all the fun things they're doing with their babies, and I'll feel like I'm just not measuring up. Like, I'm not having fun, and I'm not enjoying this time with my baby like I'm supposed to. And that just makes me feel even more anxious and overwhelmed. So, yeah, looking forward to things with enjoyment? That's not really something I've been doing lately.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes. That's something I've been doing a lot of lately. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something, whether it's because the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, or because I didn't get the laundry done, or because I forgot to buy something at the store. It's like, no matter what happens, I always find a way to twist it around and make it my fault. 

And it's not just little things, either. I'll be thinking about my baby's development, and I'll worry that I'm not doing enough to stimulate her, or that I'm not feeding her the right foods, or that I'm not giving her enough attention. And then I'll start feeling guilty and blaming myself for not being a better mom. 

It's hard to explain, but it's like I have this constant voice in my head that's always criticizing me and telling me that I'm not good enough. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always trying to prove to myself that I'm a good mom, but no matter what I do, I always seem to come up short. 

Sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me and tell me that I'm doing a great job, but it's hard for me to believe him. I feel like he's just saying that to be nice, and that deep down, he must be thinking that I'm not good enough, either. 

It's like, I know that everyone makes mistakes, and that it's okay not to be perfect. But for some reason, I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I'm always to blame, and that I'm just not good enough. It's really hard to deal with, and it's making me feel really down on myself.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes. That's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something that might happen to her. Like, I'll think about her getting sick or hurt, or about something bad happening to her when I'm not around. And it's not just rational worries, either - it's like, my mind will start spinning all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll get really caught up in them. 

Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby stops breathing? What if there's a fire in the house? What if someone breaks in and hurts us? It's like, I know these things are unlikely, but my mind just can't seem to shake them off. 

And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my husband, too - like, what if he gets hurt at work, or what if he leaves me? It's like, I know he loves me and the baby, but my mind just can't seem to stop worrying about all the things that could go wrong. 

It's hard to explain, but it's like my mind is always "on" - like, I'm always on high alert, waiting for something bad to happen. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always on edge, always waiting for the other shoe to drop. 

Sometimes, I'll try to calm myself down by telling myself that everything is okay, that the baby is safe, and that my husband loves me. But it's hard to shake off the feeling of anxiety, you know? It's like, it's always lurking there, just beneath the surface, waiting to pounce. 

I've even caught myself checking on the baby constantly, just to make sure she's breathing, or that she's not too hot or too cold. And I know it's irrational, but I just can't seem to help myself. It's like, my mind is always racing, always worrying about something or other.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be doing something normal, like feeding the baby or taking a shower, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. It's like, my heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. And it's not like I'm thinking about anything specific that's scary - it's just this general feeling of panic and fear. 

Sometimes, it's triggered by something small, like a loud noise or a sudden movement. But other times, it just seems to come out of nowhere. And it's so overwhelming - I feel like I'm going to lose control or something. 

I've had a few times where I've been holding the baby and I've felt this panic come on, and I've had to hand her to my husband because I felt like I was going to drop her or something. It's like, I know I'm a capable person, but in those moments, I just feel so out of control. 

It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, even though there isn't one. And it's not just the physical feelings - it's the emotional ones too. I'll feel like I'm going to cry or scream or something, and I just don't know how to calm myself down. 

Sometimes, I'll try to take some deep breaths or go for a walk or something, but it's hard to shake off the feeling of panic once it's started. And it's scary, because I don't know what's causing it or how to make it stop. 

I've even had a few times where I've felt like I was going to hurt myself, just because the feelings of panic and anxiety were so overwhelming. It's not like I really wanted to hurt myself, but it's just that the feelings were so intense, and I didn't know how to cope with them. It's been really scary, to be honest.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a full-time job, and on top of that, I'm trying to manage the household, and cook meals, and do laundry... it's just endless. And sometimes, I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. 

And it's not just the practical things, either. Emotionally, I'm feeling really overwhelmed, too. I'm trying to navigate this new role as a mom, and figure out who I am now, and it's just... a lot. Sometimes, I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, like I'm just disappearing into motherhood. 

I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of overwhelm wash over me. Like, I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it's just too much. I'll feel like I'm going to cry, or scream, or just run away or something. 

And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be able to handle all of this. I'm a mom now, and moms are supposed to be capable and competent, right? But the truth is, I'm just not feeling very capable or competent most of the time. I'm feeling like I'm just winging it, and hoping that I don't mess everything up. 

Sometimes, my husband will try to help me out, or offer to take the baby for a few hours, and it's like... I don't know, it's just hard for me to accept help, I guess. I feel like I'm supposed to be able to do all of this on my own, and that if I'm not, then I'm failing somehow. But at the same time, I know that I need help, and that it's okay to ask for it. It's just... it's all really confusing, and overwhelming, and hard.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just feeling anxious and unhappy. 

It's like, my mind won't turn off, and I'll just be lying there, thinking about all the things that are worrying me. And it's not just about the baby, either - it's about everything. I'll think about my relationship with my husband, and whether we're doing okay. I'll think about my own identity, and who I am now that I'm a mom. I'll think about the future, and all the things that could go wrong. 

And it's hard, because I know that sleep is important, especially when you're taking care of a new baby. But no matter how tired I am, I just can't seem to shut my mind off and relax. I'll try to focus on my breathing, or listen to calming music, but nothing seems to work. 

Sometimes, I'll get up in the middle of the night and just walk around the house, trying to clear my head. Or I'll go sit in the nursery and watch the baby sleep, just to feel some sense of peace. But even that doesn't always work, and I'll just end up feeling more anxious and overwhelmed. 

It's like, I'm trapped in this cycle of unhappiness and anxiety, and I don't know how to escape. And the lack of sleep just makes everything worse, you know? It's like, I'm already feeling fragile and emotional, and then I'm exhausted on top of it, and it's just... it's a really hard place to be. 

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to explain. He'll just tell me to try to relax, or to focus on the positive things, but it's not that easy. It's like, I know he's trying to help, but he doesn't really get it. He doesn't understand what it's like to be in my shoes, and to feel this way.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I know I'm supposed to be happy and grateful to have a new baby, and I am, but at the same time, I just feel so overwhelmed and anxious all the time. 

It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. Or I'll be feeding her, and I'll feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's not just about the baby, either - it's about everything. I'll think about my life, and how it's changed, and I'll feel sad about all the things I've lost. I'll think about my relationship with my husband, and I'll worry that we're growing apart. 

Sometimes, I'll try to talk to my husband about how I'm feeling, but it's hard to put into words. I'll just feel like I'm being a burden, or that I'm not being a good enough mom. And then I'll feel guilty for feeling that way, and it's just... it's a really hard place to be. 

I've even had thoughts about not being a good enough mom, or about not being able to take care of the baby. And those thoughts are just devastating, you know? They make me feel like I'm failing, and that I'm not worthy of love or happiness. 

It's hard, because I know I'm not alone in feeling this way. I've talked to other moms, and they've all said that they've felt the same way at some point or another. But it's hard to remember that when you're in the middle of it, you know? It's hard to remember that it's okay to feel sad, and that it's okay to not be okay. 

Sometimes, I'll have a good day, and I'll feel like I'm getting back on track. But then the next day, I'll wake up and feel miserable again. And it's just... it's a really hard cycle to break, you know? It's like, I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll just start crying. Sometimes it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and sometimes it's because I'm feeling sad or anxious. But either way, it's just... it's really hard to stop once I start. 

I've been crying about everything, too. I'll cry about the baby, and how hard it is to take care of her. I'll cry about my relationship with my husband, and how we're not connecting like we used to. I'll cry about my own identity, and how I'm not sure who I am anymore. 

Sometimes, I'll be crying, and my husband will try to comfort me, but it's hard for him to understand what I'm going through. He'll say things like, "You're a great mom," or "You're doing a great job," but it's not that simple. It's not just about being a good mom - it's about being a good person, and feeling like I'm worthy of love and happiness. 

I've even cried about stupid things, like the laundry, or the dishes. It's like, I'll just be standing there, staring at the sink, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of tears come over me. And it's not even about the dishes, really - it's about all the other things that are bothering me, and how I just feel so overwhelmed all the time. 

It's hard, because I feel like I'm crying all the time, and it's just... it's really exhausting. I feel like I'm losing control, and that I'm not able to manage my emotions like I used to. And it's scary, because I don't know how to stop it. I don't know how to make the tears stop, or how to make the sadness go away. 

But at the same time, it's kind of a relief, you know? It's like, I'm finally allowing myself to feel all the emotions that I've been trying to suppress. I'm finally giving myself permission to not be okay, and to just feel whatever it is that I'm feeling. And that's... that's a really liberating thing, I think.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I'm so sorry to say that yes, those thoughts have crossed my mind. It's like, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and hopeless, I'll think about how it would be easier if I just weren't here anymore. It's not that I really want to hurt myself, it's just that the pain and the sadness feel so overwhelming, and I don't know how to make it stop. 

It's scary, because I know that those thoughts are not okay. I know that I'm a mom now, and that I have a responsibility to take care of my baby. But at the same time, it's hard to shake off the feeling that I'm just not doing a good enough job, and that I'm not worthy of love or happiness. 

I've had thoughts about how I could just disappear, and how that would solve all my problems. But then I think about my baby, and how she needs me, and how I couldn't possibly leave her behind. And that's what keeps me going, I guess. That's what keeps me from acting on those thoughts. 

It's hard to talk about this, because it feels so shameful. It feels like I'm admitting to something that's wrong, or that I'm flawed in some way. But at the same time, I know that I need to be honest about how I'm feeling, because that's the only way I can get help. 

I just wish that I could get to a place where I feel like I'm okay, you know? Where I feel like I'm doing a good enough job, and that I'm worthy of love and happiness. I wish that I could shake off these thoughts, and just be happy and content. But until then, I guess I just have to keep talking about it, and trying to find ways to make it better.
